correctness.rationale: For alpha>1 the first update maps every initially biomass-one site to zero and every initially biomass-two site to biomass one. At the second update, the sign of 1-alpha*s/2, where s is the number of initially biomass-two neighbors, yields the complete three-regime local classification. Maximal initial two-runs force isolated survivors or independent adjacent dimers. Exact two-state updates prove periodicity below alpha=2 and stationarity at and above alpha=2. Distinct modulo-n neighboring sites and four-site patterns hold for n>=4. Independent Bernoulli bits give survival probabilities 3/8 and 1/8 and dimer probability 1/16 per start. The probability of extinction and bound for an oscillator follow from direct counting of positive initial states. The exact-rational program completed 14,224 case checks on sizes four through ten; these tests support rather than replace the universal argument.

value.rationale: Cycle graphs are the canonical one-dimensional regular habitat networks, and capacity two is the primary illustrative regime of the source model. The exact all-initial-state attraction and strict parameter thresholds quantify ecological fragmentation and distinguish fixed pairs from persistent synchronized biomass oscillations, which is more informative than a routine isolated numerical example. Exact 3/8 versus 1/8 finite-cycle survival and almost-sure large-cycle oscillation provide natural calibrations for network-phase and dynamic-cavity studies. The theorem does not claim generality beyond its meaningful solvable benchmark.
